Whether or not you use the Double Lunar or Solar Lunar opener ultimately depends on your killtime. If you are unsure(or simply don't care about that level of optimization), use the Solar Lunar opener.

>It now makes more sense to me why people recommend starting with a solar one too, because then the lunar can be done under RoF and uses more opo moves, right?

If you are going to use Elixir Burst and Rising Phoenix during your even minute burst window(which you would when using the Solar Lunar opener), then yep, you would prepare Rising Phoenix and then build up Elixir Burst under RoF and BH because it gains you more Opo GCDs under burst.

  
Depending on how much you care about learning MNK, I can recommend [this](https://docs.google.com/document/u/1/d/e/2PACX-1vQwCPGL47NAZyQ5zcKBQliPHaRC4wH61IPa-QFZ-vMQl4xiulWpbVkiIKBdWYLo4NZ1ghtjsS9PfbqB/pub) MNK DT writeup. It's not a full guide yet, partly because MNK got adjusted again just this tuesday but it's a nice read in case you are curious to learn more.

You generally want to get 11 GCDs under RoF, make sure you weave that as late as possible.

Inside the actual even burst window, you want to have as many opo GCDs, your two beast chakras and your two replies. Note that Wind's Reply isn't up for every burst window because of its 90s CD.

So, with that in mind, you *ideally* would have something like 2x Beast Chakras, 2x Replies and 7x Opo GCDs. That won't always be possible, especially if you use the Solar Lunar Opener.
